memories.memory_text: I saw Holden stand up and call out, challenging Hooper by saying that Lando Calrissian was a positive black role model in science fiction.
I was there when Hooper told Banky to shut up during his speech, cutting him off completely and making it clear he wasn't going to entertain his question.
I saw Hooper pull a gun and shoot Banky, and I was terrified until he broke character and revealed it was all an act with blanks, approved by his publisher.
I saw Hooper break character and kiss Banky on the lips, and then Banky wiped his mouth and made it clear he wasn't interested in anything more than acting.
I shoved and slapped Hooper because he kept cutting me off on panels, always speaking before I could get a word in—I finally snapped and told him exactly how fed up I was.
I was part of the 'Words Up - Minority Voices in Comics' panel at the convention, and I got frustrated because I never got to speak before Hooper's act ended things again.
I mocked Banky when I found out he's just an inker, telling him he only traces, and I could see how it got under his skin.

I remember when Holden told me he enjoyed my book and was surprised we hadn't met at other cons before—I shot back with a sarcastic remark about him losing the dick or changing his skin tone if he wanted to get to know me, just to keep the flirtation sharp and on my terms.
I heard Hooper say 'Archie and Jughead were lovers,' and I saw Banky immediately snap and yell, 'Shut the fuck up!'
I remember Holden siding with Hooper by saying Archie never chose between Betty or Veronica, which I could tell only made Banky more upset.
I was at the bar with Holden, Banky, and Hooper, drinking, talking, and just hanging out like we often do.
I watched Banky decide to go across the street to buy a bunch of Archie comics to prove once and for all that Archie was only interested in girls.
I told Holden that what he was seeing wasn't love, I said that out there was just fleeting, not real love.

I shared my mother's uncle's story with them—I remembered how he found silver ingots, became a millionaire, and then lost everything when his fiancée was murdered; I still recall how he rode that train every day for the rest of his life, donating his fortune to light the station, and how I told them, 'That's my love story.'
I saw that couple out the window, right there on the hood of Banky's car, and I knew it wasn't love—I said so, that it was just fleeting, nothing real.
I joined the group as we began leaving the bar, feeling the night wind when I stepped out into the dark.
I remember Hooper saying, with a smirk, that Mister Weatherbee was Reggie's bitch—suddenly flipping the whole Archie power structure on its head when Holden asked about it.
I remember Holden telling Banky that we shared a meaningful moment and that I love him, though I didn't hear it directly from me.
I heard Banky make a sarcastic comment about my dancing, something about Denny Terrio that made me feel mocked.
I remember when Holden thought I had a boyfriend, but someone corrected him—I don't recall who—saying I wasn't in a relationship, and that made things easier for him.
I hoped Holden would come after I asked Hooper to invite him, and when he showed up at the club, I felt sure he came for me.
I remember when Holden bumped into me on the dance floor and pretended to be mad about his cabbage-patch, which made me laugh and call him Mister Home-Town himself.
I told Hooper to invite Holden to the club, and later I knew he had called because I said, 'I know. Hooper told me.'

I realized I knew overlapping people from home when Holden mentioned Highlands and Hudson, and we started trading stories about the tri-town area, Quick Stop, and the Y.M.C.A. pool, which made me say I was a dangerous person to know.

I was stunned when the singer revealed I used to be in the band and invited me to perform—everyone was staring, and I initially shook my head no, but then I thought, why not, and I got up and said I should dedicate the song, maybe to that special someone out there.
After my song, I pointed to a woman in the audience and beckoned her with a 'c'mere' gesture, feeling the moment pull me toward her.

I took the microphone and performed a song, feeling the energy build as I made eye contact with someone in the crowd and curled my finger in a 'c'mere' motion—I remember thinking, 'I should dedicate this,' and saying it was for 'that special someone out there,' letting the moment hang with all its uncertainty.
I pulled her into my arms and we shared a kiss that was too passionate to mean anything but what it was—I knew it changed things, especially for Holden.
I remember the club buzzing around me, people moving, music playing, and me dancing right in the middle of it all, feeling the energy as we celebrated the band.
I saw Banky mimic Holden's smile and sarcastically comment on how Holden thought we had a romantic connection, as if he knew better.

I remember Banky pressing me with that crude question about how girls can 'fuck' each other, like it had to involve strap-ons or some gimmick—he really seemed fixated on getting some kind of 'inside scoop' from me.

I told Banky that 'fucking' isn't just about penetration—it's about the intent, not the act. I explained that for me, it means sex without love, like when I sleep with Kim, and I pointed out he probably doesn't love every girl he sleeps with either.

I was drunk sophomore year, going down on Cynthia Slater in her dorm after club-hopping, and I fell asleep right in her lap—I remember waking up to her digging her heel into my back, and I still have the scar from it.
I felt Kim's lips on my neck when she came back into the bar, that soft kiss telling me she was still with me.
I heard Holden say they had to leave to beat traffic, and I saw Banky slide out of the booth before Holden pulled him out as they headed for the door.

I was just trying to stay seated, telling Kim I’d rather watch, but she kept pushing—then later, after all the talk and laughter with Holden and Banky, I realized it was just part of that easy, messy night out with friends, full of stories and good humor.
I chose to stay behind with Kim, and after watching Holden and Banky go, I turned to her and kissed her, feeling the shift in the night's momentum.
I remember Kim tugging my arm and insisting I join her on the dance floor, her touch warm and insistent, making it clear she wanted us to share that moment together in public.
I arrived at the studio and knocked on the door, waiting for someone to answer.

I pitched my story idea to Holden about a man who runs away when he finds out a girl is a sex worker, drawing from something I know too well, and I was hoping he’d be interested in working on it with me.

I heard Holden say he wasn't happy with how commercial M-TV had become and that he wanted to go back to doing something more personal, like their first book, and I could sense how much that mattered to him.
I told Holden I find him handsome, not just because of how he looks, but because of his outlook and the way he sees things—I meant it when I said it's genuinely attractive to me.

I remember when Holden asked me why I'm attracted to girls, and I realized he assumed liking girls meant I must hate men. I told him that girls just feel right to me, and I've never really been drawn to men—I'm more comfortable with the idea of being with girls. He pointed out I've only been with girls, but that didn't shake how I feel.

I challenged Holden when he kept referring to 'the standard' definition of virginity, because I believe I lose my virginity when I make love for the first time, not just based on some biological or heteronormative rule that ignores emotional experience.

I explained to Holden how attraction and sex between women go beyond looks, and when he seemed skeptical about lesbian sexual adequacy, I showed him what I meant by letting my tongue out—it was surprising, even to me, how stunned he looked.

I remember walking with Holden through the riverside park, eating hot dogs and then sitting on the swings, talking about art, identity, and sexuality—our conversation felt deep and personal, and I could tell he was really thinking about things in a new way.

I remember telling Holden I was staying all weekend and wanted to hang out, and he decided to skip the convention to be with me instead—he even arranged to pick me up from my friend's apartment in the Village, saying he'd be there in half an hour.
I remember when the trip to Dragon Con was supposed to be something Holden and Banky were both going to do, but now it's just Banky going.

I arrived at Alyssa's apartment to pick her up, and when the door opened, a woman standing there in her bra looked me up and down and smirked before mocking me for thinking I could be 'the right man' who'd save her from being a lesbian, challenging everything I believed about us.

I stepped in to calm things down between Holden and my friend, telling him not to mind her harsh words because that's just her way of saying hello, even though she insisted she was serious about warning him.
I teased Holden by sticking out my tongue and saying 'Remember this!' then joked that my friend's tongue is even bigger, knowing it would make him uncomfortable and lighten the mood.

I remember realizing that my shift from trying to fit in to living more authentically wasn't something that happened overnight—it was gradual, shaped by all sorts of moments, like how I was raised, how kids treated me in school, even the shoes I wore to my freshman prom.

I remember talking with Holden about religion while we were driving, and when he asked if I had a strict upbringing, I told him I was raised Baptist and how we were always saying 'Jesus'—there was no time to be bad.
I teased Holden by miming how to insert a tampon after I noticed him getting flustered when I added them to our shopping cart.

I was trying to light my cigarette in the studio, but the lighter had a child-proof tab and I couldn't get it off. Holden noticed, grabbed the lighter, and pulled the tab out with his teeth—then lit my cigarette for me. I just stared at him, a little taken aback.
I took Holden's hand and pulled his arm around my shoulder in the parking lot.
I corrected Holden when he said we were both into girls—I told him I'm into women, not girls, because that feels more accurate to who I am.
I recall reflecting with Holden about our chemistry and how we both ended up into girls, and I even mentioned my crush on Scott Baio when I was nine, like it was part of figuring myself out.
I remember saying that even back in high school, I would have been attracted to women—I knew myself well enough that it wasn't just a phase or something that changed over time.

I couldn't help but tease them, so I said something sarcastic about how guys who play hockey are just compensating for penile deficiencies with big sticks—I thought it was funny how seriously they took the game.
I remember Banky mocking me for showing up at the studio so often, even though I said I lived in the city—he brought up some 'little pink mafia' like I was breaking some rule just by being there.
I walked in and saw Holden and Banky hunched over the Sega, totally focused on their hockey game, slapping at the controls like it was some kind of sacred ritual.
I heard Holden sarcastically say that it was the controller's fault, like it's always the controller's fault, not Banky's skill.

I stood beside Holden and Banky while they played hockey, and I saw Banky get furious when he lost—he started yelling at the screen and blaming the controls and his teammates before finally throwing his controller and storming off.
I saw Banky storm off, and then I looked at Holden just as he made that dry comment about how it would've been different if he'd only won by one point instead of thirty.
I saw Holden mock Banky for being slow during the hockey game, saying he moved like a geriatric and blaming the controller, and then after Banky stormed off, Holden joked about how much he'd won by.
I threw the ball overhand and it rebounded dangerously, so Holden told me to throw underhand for better control.
I teased Holden about taking 'straight chicks' on dates to a skee-ball arcade, wondering if he thought that was romantic.
I spent time with Holden at the skee-ball arcade, where we played casually and talked while he introduced me to the game.
I confronted Holden about his friend using homophobic slurs during their game, telling him that even if it seems casual, it still reflects a deeper intolerance that I can't just ignore.

I explained to Holden that when marginalized people reclaim slurs, it's about taking back power and masking pain, but when someone outside that experience uses those words, it's just hurtful and shows a lack of awareness.
I told Holden about getting laid last night, and he got so startled that he threw a skee-ball up into the ceiling—it bounced off and shattered the glass on a pinball machine.
I was having a meal with Holden at the diner, and after our conversation took a turn, I decided it was time to leave and told him I had some business to conduct.

I approached the cashier and asked if he had the authority to negotiate, then made him an offer of fifty dollars for the painting I wanted; even though I gave my name and he called that a mistake, I stayed firm and ended up buying it for twenty-five dollars.
I negotiated with the cashier and bought the painting for twenty-five dollars, making sure to close the deal before revealing it to Holden.
I told Holden in the car that the painting is a gift from me to him, meant to symbolize our friendship and remind him of our moments together.

I remember Holden stopping the car and telling me he loves me—really loves me—in a way that’s not just friendly, saying it’s genuine and life-changing, and that he’s been holding it in for so long he couldn’t keep silent anymore, even if it meant losing our friendship.
After he said everything, I didn’t know what to say, so I stayed silent, just looked at him, and then I got out of the car without speaking.
I remember walking up the road when Holden called out, asking me what I was doing.
I told Holden to fuck off after he dropped that emotional bomb on me.
I was standing there in the rain when Holden told me he was in love with me, his voice shaking a little.
I told Holden it was unfair for him to dump his feelings on me, that he needs to remember who I am — I can't just enter a relationship with him without turning my whole world upside down.
I hit Holden when he talked about a 'period of adjustment' — I shouted at him that there's no adjustment period, that I'm gay and he can't expect me to change just because he has a crush on me.
I walked away from Holden, but then I turned back and pounced on him, grabbing his face and kissing him deeply, giving in to something I didn't fully understand.
I remember the whole thing—the yelling, the rain, me pushing him away, then later pulling him into a kiss that surprised us both.
I was sleeping under a blanket with Holden when I suddenly woke up, startled, and saw Banky standing there looking completely shocked.
I was startled awake by Banky's reaction, and then Holden told me to stay, kissed me, and left the studio.
I felt cornered when Dalia suddenly confronted me, asking why I was playing the pronoun game, like she knew I was hiding something about the person I’ve been seeing.
I took a breath and told them I’m in a romantic relationship with Holden, someone from my hometown, and I’ll never forget how quiet the room got when I said his name.
I told the group about dating Holden, and right after, Dalia and Jane got up and left the gathering without really saying why.
I remember that night when Tory, Nica, Dalia, and Jane all came over to help me finish an issue of 'Idiosyncratic Routine' in my living room, laughing and working together.
I saw Tory raise her glass with a sarcastic 'here's to both of you' after Dalia and Jane left, and I could tell she wasn't happy about my relationship.

I remember lying in Holden's arms after we made love, moonlight filling the room, and feeling safe enough to tell him the truth about why I chose him—not because of what society expected, but because I refused to limit my chances of finding that one person who truly gets me, and I found him on my own terms.
I corrected Holden when he joked that he was the 'right man' who saved me, because I needed to make it clear—he's not my savior, he's the one I chose, and I didn't need to be converted or fixed.
I think Holden took the tape from me because he noticed an older woman staring at me, and I felt like he was uncomfortable with me holding it.
I was looking at the back of a lesbian porn tape when Holden took it from my hands and ushered me away.

I used my hands to guide Holden, waving him left and right until he finally got the painting just right — it took a few tries, with it crooked at first and then upside down, but I stayed patient and kept directing him until I could lean back against the wall, smiling and closing my eyes in quiet satisfaction.

I remember all the little moments we shared—playing video games, walking in the park, hanging my painting in his apartment—that showed me how real this is, not because of any rule or label, but because being with him just feels right.

I heard Holden talking to Hooper about that rumor Banky spread, and he admitted it got to him—how I’d supposedly been with two guys at once. I can tell it’s bothering him, even though he tries to play it off.

I saw Hooper shift into this militant, politically charged persona when a young Black kid came up to him for a comic signing—he greeted him with 'A-salaam Alaikum, little brother' and started talking about the Man and staying vigilant, telling the kid to 'fight the power'—but the moment the boy walked away, I noticed him slip back into his real voice and quietly express how he felt pressured to perform just to earn respect.
I was really into the hockey game, enjoying every moment while sitting in the bleachers with fans all around us, but I could tell Holden wasn't sharing my excitement.
I called Holden out on his 'cross-examination'—that's what he was really doing, badgering me like a witness instead of just asking me openly.

I felt cornered when Holden started grilling me about my old yearbook nickname 'Finger Cuffs' and brought up Rick Derris, implying things about my past that made me defensive—I told him if he wanted to know about me, he could’ve just asked instead of playing detective.

I told Holden about the time Rick pulled out his dick and chased me around the house with it, right in front of Cohee, and how I ended up blowing him while Cohee fucked me — I couldn't believe he'd push me like that, so I threw it in his face to shut him down.
After I confronted him, I gathered my things and stormed out, I wasn't going to stay in that game and let him treat me like that.
I told Holden the truth—I admitted that all the rumors about me were true, including having sex with two guys at once, cheating on prom, and the videotaped incident in college.
I told him he was the missing piece I’d been searching for, that being with him made me feel whole, because I wanted him to understand how much he meant to me.
I reached for his face, and I felt him pull away, like I’d burned him.
I called him out on his hypocrisy—I told him it made no sense that he’s fine with me sleeping with half the women in New York but judges me for things I did as a teenager.
I lashed out at him, defending myself fiercely because I was tired of being judged—he had no right to act so hypocritical after everything he’s done.
He told me he wants us to be something we can’t, that he wants us to be a 'normal couple,' like that was some kind of death sentence for what we are.
After Holden left, I kicked and punched the car beside me, screaming into the air, and then I just collapsed to the ground, sobbing.
I remember storming out of the rink and into the parking lot, pulling on my coat, with Holden chasing after me to confront me about my past.
I saw Holden toss an envelope to Jay, and I figured it must've had the payment and a comic inside, since that’s what he owed them.
I remember when Holden told Jay and Silent Bob about us, how he said my name like it meant something real.

I can feel the weight in his voice when he talked about loving me but struggling with my past, how he said he sees kids and grandkids when he looks at me, yet still can't let go of things like 'Finger Cuffs'.
I remember Jay complaining about how the comic made him sound, saying the dialogue wasn't like real life and calling 'snootchie-bootchies' baby-talk.
I was sitting on the couch with Banky when Holden brought us together, pacing in front of us, saying he wanted to settle things between us.
I remember Holden telling Banky directly, 'You're in love with me,' and explaining that Banky had been repressing his feelings for him.
I saw Holden grab Banky and kiss him forcefully on the lips, pushing him back onto the couch, and I reacted in shock while Banky just sat there speechless.

I remember when Holden proposed that we all have sex together—he said it would fix everything between us, that it would make him feel less inadequate, help Banky take that leap, and dissolve the tension so we could stay together.
I remember Holden pressing me to agree to the threesome, saying it was necessary for our relationship and for us to grow, like it was something I owed him and us just to stay together.

I told Holden that I've been down these roads before and found nothing in them, that doing this threesome would only create more problems and damage us — I can't go back to that life, not even for him.
I hugged Holden, trying to hold onto the love one last time, but then I slapped him — my anger and sense of betrayal had to be felt, not just spoken.
After telling him I couldn't be part of this or him anymore, I walked out of the studio and closed the door behind me, knowing I wouldn't be coming back.
I saw Holden hold up Banky's comic and give him a thumbs up, and I remember thinking how quiet it was—no words, just that gesture, like they finally found a way back to each other.
I remember Holden asking me to call him with my thoughts after I looked through his comic, and I said okay, feeling like this might be the start of something between us again.
I was at my signing table when Holden showed up and gave me a copy of his self-published comic, 'Chasing Amy'—it surprised me, but I could tell he meant it as a way to reconnect.
I was at a comic book convention a year after everything changed, sitting at my own signing table and signing copies of my comic while fans waited in line.

memories.memory_text: I saw our comic, the second issue of 'Bluntman and Chronic,' sitting right there on the shelf for the first time.
I pointed out to Holden that both our names were on the cover—Banky Edwards and Holden McNeil—and I felt proud as hell.

I couldn't believe Steve-Dave and Walt tore into our comic like that, calling it mediocre and a piece of shit, and saying we were no-talents who got lucky—I felt my face burn as they mocked me and Holden right there at the counter.
As we turned to leave, I saw Steve-Dave flip us off, both middle fingers up, before going back to his game like we were nothing—I clenched my fists but kept walking.
I went to the comic store with Holden to buy our newly released issue, and I remember nudging him before we left after making the purchase.
I saw the trash can come flying through the store's front window, shattering the glass.
Someone told me that a check for three times the window's cost was left with a mocking note addressed to me, saying 'Kiss it, Banky the Hack.'
I told the collector that inking isn't tracing—I add depth and shading that give the drawing its real shape, and that's a creative act I'm proud of.
A collector kept insisting that inking is just tracing, which really got under my skin and felt like he was dismissing everything I do.

I offered to sign my name for the kid, but he yanked the book back and said, 'I don't want you to sign it, I want the guy that draws Bluntman and Chronic to sign it. You're just a tracer,'—just like the Collector mocked me.
I was at a comic book convention signing copies of 'Bluntman and Chronic' with Holden, and fans kept coming up, excited to meet us and have their books signed.
I lost control and throttled the Collector across the table after he kept belittling my art—I couldn't take the insults anymore.

I remember Holden scolding me about how I alienated the fans, saying that if I keep antagonizing the audience, we won't have one left—and he even held up his watch to remind me the curtain was in ten minutes.
